chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about al-Qāʾim, so he said:
All of us are قائم by the command of Allah, one after another, until the Owner of the Sword comes. Then when the Owner of the Sword comes, he will come with a matter other than that which had been.

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: the one who rises by divine command; here, discussed in relation to the Imams عليهم السلام and the final Qa'im
key_terms.بِأَمْرٍ غَيْرِ الَّذِي كَانَ: with a matter other than that which had been; indicating a distinct mode or phase of divinely commanded rule
key_terms.بِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ: by the command of Allah; indicating divinely authorized authority and mission
key_terms.صَاحِبُ السَّيْفِ: the Owner of the Sword; a title for the Imam whose rise is marked by manifest action
key_terms.وَاحِدٌ بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ: one after another; describing the successive continuity of the Imams عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: How do the Imams عليهم السلام describe al-Qāʾim and the coming of the صاحب السيف?
ai.summary: The hadith explains that each Imam عليه السلام upholds the command of Allah in succession. It distinguishes the final Qa'im, the صاحب السيف, whose divinely mandated rise will bring a new phase of manifest authority and action.
